C1.1.1a.q: Every quarter, a firm plans new security controls, puts them in place, checks how well they worked, then improves them. Which approach is this?
options: Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle in the cyber security policy
C1.1.1a.why: The cyber security policy runs as a repeating Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle (ISO 27001).

C1.1.1b.q: A company bans staff from downloading .exe files and warns them that work email may be monitored. Which policy sets these rules?
C1.1.1b.why: The internet and email use policy defines acceptable internet and email use at work.

C1.1.1c.q: The system blocks 'Password123' and locks an account after five failed logins. Which part of policy does this enforce?
C1.1.1c.why: Security and password procedures enforce strong passwords and safe account use.

C1.1.1d.q: All staff must complete annual phishing training and report suspicious emails to IT. Which part of the policy is this?
C1.1.1d.why: This part sets out what staff must do for security and how they are trained.

C1.1.2.q: A review finds three ex-employees whose accounts are still active, which breaks the company's own leavers policy. What process found this?
C1.1.2.why: A security audit checks that the organisation follows its own security policies and the law.

C1.1.3.q: A document states that incrementals run nightly, full backups weekly, and restores are tested every quarter by the IT manager. Which policy is this?
C1.1.3.why: A backup policy states what is backed up, how, how often and by whom.

C1.1.4.q: A company appoints a Data Protection Officer and makes contractors follow GDPR rules when handling customer data. Which policy is this?
C1.1.4.why: The data protection policy makes sure the organisation follows data protection law.

C1.1.5.q: Ransomware is detected. Staff follow a triage flowchart and contact list covering legal, PR, HR and insurers. Which policy are they following?
C1.1.5.why: The incident response policy is the plan for responding to a security incident.

C1.1.6.q: A fire destroys a company's head office. The policy guides how systems and operations are restored at a backup site. Which policy is this?
C1.1.6.why: Disaster recovery restores systems and operations after a major disruption.

C1.1.7.q: A school's contract with its IT support company sets a 4-hour response time and fines if fixes are late. Which policy covers this?
C1.1.7.why: The external services policy governs outside providers, often through a service level agreement.
